findings.title: Fallback locale files are not loaded on translate
findings.body: The on-demand loader in I18n.translate only calls load_locale for config.locale. FallbackLocaleList and I18n::Backend::Fallbacks then look up SiteSetting.default_locale and :en, but those YAML files stay unloaded unless something else has called ensure_loaded!. The only call site is ApplicationController#set_locale, so jobs, mailers, models, middleware, and I18n.with_locale blocks never load the fallback chain. Missing keys then raise or return the Rails "translation missing" string instead of the site-locale or English string. Because translate also LRU-caches that result (and the production exception handler returns a string rather than raising), a miss can stick in the cache even after the fallback files are loaded later in the same process.

findings.title: Translation cache ignores the fallback chain
findings.body: The LRU key is only "#{key}#{config.locale}#{config.backend.object_id}". With fallbacks enabled, the cached string can come from SiteSetting.default_locale or :en, but the key does not include that chain. default_locale is an admin-changeable runtime setting; after it changes, locales that were missing the key keep serving the previous fallback language until the 300-entry cache evicts the entry. ensure_loaded! loading the new locale file does not invalidate those entries.

findings.title: No tests for fallback order or locale loading
findings.body: The new FallbackLocaleList (user locale, then SiteSetting.default_locale, then :en) and the ensure_loaded! hook are untested. Nothing asserts that a key missing in the user locale resolves to the site locale before English, that string/symbol locales collapse, or that a translation outside ApplicationController#set_locale still loads fallback YAML. Those are the paths this change is most likely to get wrong, and a regression would ship user-visible missing or wrong strings.
